findings.title: Sudoers rule grants root-equivalent access despite its "nothing wider" claim
findings.description:
`MT_INSTALL` allows `manta` to run `/home/manta/source/repos/manta/trading-data/deploy/install-production.sh --ref *` as root with no password. That script lives in a directory the `manta` user can write to. Anyone with that account can edit the script and then run it as root, so the rule is full root, not a limited grant.

The unit globs (`systemctl stop mt-*` and the other three) and `mt-run *` also use sudoers `*`. That wildcard matches spaces and extra arguments, so any option the wrapper or `systemctl` accepts is allowed. The header comment says the rule grants "exactly the commands those scripts issue", which is not true of these entries.

Fixes:
- Run the installer from a root-owned path such as `/usr/local/sbin`.
- Pin the `--ref` argument.
- Confirm what arguments `mt-run` accepts.
- Replace the unit globs with explicit unit names.

findings.title: Cagg freshness compares a refresh finish time to a bar write time
findings.description:
`stale` is `last_refresh < newest_bar_written`, where `last_refresh` is `last_successful_finish`. A refresh that started before the last bar was written but finished after it passes as fresh, even though the cagg never materialized that bar. `last_successful_start` is the safer comparison.

Two further assumptions are unverified:
- That `job.hypertable_name = cagg` matches the cagg refresh policy row in `timescaledb_information.jobs`. If it does not, `last_refresh` is always `None`, `--verify` reports `[WAIT]` forever, and the cutover can never pass.
- That the refresh policy window covers the judged session.

The tests mock the cursor, so none of this is exercised against a real database.

findings.title: Per-session judgement can keep a gap row forever for a symbol with no bars in a session
findings.description: The old weekend and holiday tolerance is replaced by "every session in the chunk must hold a bar". A halted, newly listed or illiquid symbol can legitimately have no bars for a whole session. Its chunk then returns PARTIAL on every pass, the row is kept, and `attempt_count` climbs. That is the "re-fetches forever" behavior the removed comment described. Cap the retries or add a staleness exit. The tests cover only the all-sessions-empty and all-sessions-covered cases.

findings.title: Extra connection per chunk on the fetch hot path
findings.description: `fetch_session_bounds` is called through a fresh `pool.connection()` on every chunk of every symbol, across a universe of thousands of symbols. Reuse the connection already open in `_do_minute_symbol`, or cache the bounds per cycle.

findings.title: Duplicated timestamp parsing, and a daemon module importing from a repair-script module
findings.description:
`bar_timestamp` re-implements `_bar_to_row`'s timestamp parsing, as `_latest_bar_dt` did before it was removed. The docstring says it "mirrors" `_bar_to_row`, which is exactly the duplication that drifts. Extract one shared parser.

The production daemon now also imports `build_truncated_day_index` and `RepairScanTimeout` from `data/gaps/repair_921.py`, a one-off repair module. Move those into a neutral gaps module. The `_UTC = UTC` alias is also unnecessary.

findings.title: "[WAIT]" and "FAIL" are string-matched across scripts with no shared definition
findings.description: The repair script prints `[WAIT]` and the cutover script searches for the literal substring in three places. The project rules say comparison values are defined once. The same applies to `"FAIL"`, which was already a pre-existing literal. Define the markers as constants in one shared module and import them into both scripts.

findings.title: Import ordering will fail ruff `I`
findings.description:
The ordering is wrong in several places:
- `NOTES_DIR, fire_unit_until, start_log` come before `CutoverError`.
- `cagg_freshness_for_session` comes before `CheckReport` in `repair_921_minute_sessions.py` and in `test_repair_921.py`.
- The new `minute_sessions` and `repair_921` imports in `minute.py` sit ahead of `minute_coverage`.

I did not check whether ruff is configured with `I` in `pyproject.toml`. If it is, the lint gate fails.

findings.title: Narration log uses module-global state and truncates on open
findings.description: `_LOG_FILE` is a mutable global. `start_log` overwrites the file, and `say` reopens it on every call. Streamed subprocess output and the bare `print` lines in `wait_for_unit_or_line` and `fire_unit_until` never reach the log. The docstring calls the narration "the cutover's report", but the log is incomplete. The timestamped filename makes the truncation low risk.

findings.title: `fire_unit_until` repeats the tail of `fire_unit`
findings.description: The cursor, start-time, `mt-run` and `sudo -v` sequence is duplicated between the two functions. A shared helper would remove it.

findings.title: Test setup is copy-pasted
findings.description:
`test_last_bar_before_the_chunk_end_is_still_success` repeats the roughly 40-line mock and patch scaffold from `_run`. Parametrize `_run` over bounds, bars and gap instead.

The timing changes are covered: firing times, 07:05 judging boundaries, the UTC label fix and the timer files all agree with the constants.

structured_findings.summary: Sudoers rule grants root-equivalent access despite its "nothing wider" claim
Cagg freshness compares a refresh finish time to a bar write time
Per-session judgement can keep a gap row forever for a symbol with no bars in a session
Extra connection per chunk on the fetch hot path
Duplicated timestamp parsing, and a daemon module importing from a repair-script module
"[WAIT]" and "FAIL" are string-matched across scripts with no shared definition
Narration log uses module-global state and truncates on open
